  • Learn about the built-in codecs for other format options.

docs.title: CLI Tools
docs.text: The Amplitude Audio SDK ships with three command-line tools for asset processing and pipeline management. This reference documents their usage, options, and exit codes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Tool Purpose Input Output amac Amplitude Audio Compressor WAV, MP3 AMS (ADPCM) or WAV amir Amplitude HRIR Sphere Builder IRCAM, MIT, SADIE, SOFA .amir file ampk Amplitude Packager Project directory .ampk package

All tools follow a consistent CLI style and support --verbose, --quiet, --no-logo, and --version flags.

docs.title: amac
docs.text:
Amplitude Audio Compressor

amac encodes standard audio files into Amplitude's custom AMS ADPCM format, or decodes AMS files back to WAV.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: amac [OPTIONS] <input_file> <output_file>

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Default Description -e, --encode — Encode mode: convert input to AMS. -d, --decode — Decode mode: convert AMS to WAV. -l, --no-logo false Hide the logo and copyright notice. -v, --verbose false Print detailed processing information. -q, --quiet false Quiet mode: suppress all output (implies --no-logo and disables verbose). -0 … -8 -3 Look-ahead level for encoding (0 = fastest/lowest quality, 8 = slowest/highest quality). Default is level 3. Encode-only. -f — Disable noise shaping during encoding. Encode-only. -b, --block-size-shift N 0 ADPCM block size exponent. Must be in the range [8, 15]; when 0, the block size is computed automatically from channel count and sample rate. Encode-only. -r, --resample FREQ — Resample input data to FREQ Hz before encoding. Accepted range: [8000, 384000]. Encode-only.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Encode a WAV to AMS (default look-ahead level 3)
amac -e input.wav output.ams

# Encode with noise shaping disabled and look-ahead level 5
amac -e -f -5 input.wav output.ams

# Encode with a custom block-size-shift
amac -e -b 12 input.wav output.ams

# Decode AMS back to WAV
amac -d input.ams output.wav

# Encode and resample to 48 kHz
amac -e -r 48000 input.wav output.ams

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Invalid arguments or file not found 2 Encoding/decoding error

docs.title: amir
docs.text:
Amplitude HRIR Sphere Builder

amir converts HRIR (Head-Related Impulse Response) datasets into Amplitude's optimized .amir sphere format for runtime HRTF spatialization.

docs.title: Supported Datasets
docs.text: Dataset Model value (-m) Source IRCAM 0 IRCAM LISTEN MIT KEMAR 1 MIT Media Lab SADIE II 2 University of York SOFA 3 SOFA Conventions

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: amir [OPTIONS] DATASET_DIR OUTPUT_FILE

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Default Description -m, --model {0,1,2,3} — (Required) Source dataset model: 0 = IRCAM, 1 = MIT KEMAR, 2 = SADIE II, 3 = SOFA. -l, --no-logo false Hide the logo and copyright notice. -v, --verbose false Print detailed processing information. -q, --quiet false Quiet mode: suppress all output (implies --no-logo and disables verbose). -d, --debug false Output a 3D visualization mesh of the HRIR sphere as debug_hrir_sphere.obj. -r, --resample FREQ — Resample IR data to FREQ Hz before writing the .amir file.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Convert a SOFA file to AMIR (model 3 = SOFA)
amir -m 3 hrtf.sofa hrtf.amir

# Convert MIT KEMAR data with resampling to 48 kHz (model 1 = MIT)
amir -m 1 -r 48000 /path/to/mit_kemar/ output.amir

# Convert IRCAM data and emit a debug visualization mesh (model 0 = IRCAM)
amir -m 0 --debug /path/to/ircam/ output.amir
# Produces output.amir + debug_hrir_sphere.obj (visualization mesh)

docs.title: Output Format
docs.text:
The .amir file contains:

  • Triangulated sphere mesh (vertices + faces)
  • Left and right ear HRIR data per vertex
  • Interaural time difference (ITD) delays
  • Sample rate and IR length metadata

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Invalid arguments or file not found 2 Processing error (invalid dataset format)

docs.title: ampk
docs.text:
Amplitude Packager

ampk packs an entire Amplitude project directory into a single .ampk file for efficient distribution and loading at runtime.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: ampk [OPTIONS] <project_dir> <output_file>

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Default Description -c, --compression {0,1} 0 Compression mode: 0 = uncompressed, 1 = LZ4. -s, --block-size N 64 Compression block size in KB. Only used when LZ4 compression is active. -l, --no-logo false Hide the logo and copyright notice. -v, --verbose false Print detailed packaging information. -q, --quiet false Quiet mode: suppress all output (implies --no-logo and disables verbose).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Create an uncompressed package
ampk ./my_project/ output.ampk

# Create an LZ4-compressed package with 128KB blocks
ampk -c 1 -s 128 ./my_project/ output.ampk

# Package verbosely
ampk -v ./my_project/ output.ampk

docs.title: Compression Modes
docs.text:
Mode Value Description Use Case Uncompressed 0 No compression; fastest load times Desktop, SSD storage LZ4 1 Fast compression and decompression Mobile, console, streaming

LZ4 compression reduces file size with minimal CPU overhead during decompression. The block size controls the compression granularity; larger blocks yield better compression but use more memory during loading.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Invalid arguments or directory not found 2 Packaging or I/O error

docs.title: Common Options
docs.text:
All three tools support these global flags:

Flag Description --version Print the tool version and exit. --help Print usage information and exit.

docs.title: Building the Tools
docs.text:
The tools are built automatically when build_tools is enabled in the XMake configuration:

xmake config --build_tools=y
xmake

Binaries are placed in the build/[platform]/[arch]/[mode]/ directory.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Learn how to set up HRTF using amir.
  • Learn how to compile Amplitude projects.
  • Explore the PackageFileSystem API for runtime package loading.

docs.title: Built-in Codecs
docs.text: This reference documents the audio codecs built into the Amplitude Audio SDK, including supported formats, capabilities, and usage notes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Amplitude includes three built-in codecs. Additional codecs are available via plugins.

Codec Extension Decoding Encoding Streaming Description WAV .wav ✅ ✅ ✅ PCM and IEEE float formats via dr_wav MP3 .mp3 ✅ ❌ ✅ MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III via dr_mp3 AMS .ams ✅ ✅ ✅ Amplitude's custom ADPCM compression

docs.title: WAV Codec
docs.text: The WAV codec supports standard RIFF/WAVE files via the dr_wav library.

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text: Format Bits Per Sample Notes PCM 8, 16, 24, 32 Integer PCM IEEE Float 32 Floating-point samples

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Decoded audio is always converted to 32-bit float (eAudioSampleFormat_Float32) internally.
  • The codec supports both full Load() and streaming Stream() modes.
  • IMA/DVI ADPCM WAV files are not handled by the WAV codec; they are routed to the AMS codec.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "gunshot",
  "path": "sounds/gunshot.wav"
}

docs.title: MP3 Codec
docs.text: The MP3 codec supports MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III decoding via dr_mp3.

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text: Format Notes MPEG-1 Layer III Standard MP3 MPEG-2 Layer III Lower sample rates

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Decoded audio is always converted to 32-bit float internally.
  • Supports streaming for long music tracks.
  • Encoding is not supported. Use external tools to create MP3 files.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
{
  "id": 2,
  "name": "music_track",
  "path": "music/background.mp3",
  "stream": true
}

docs.title: AMS Codec
docs.text: The AMS (Amplitude Media Stream) codec is Amplitude's custom ADPCM compression format. It provides a good balance between compression ratio and decoding speed.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Compression ~4:1 over 16-bit PCM Decode speed Very fast (simple ADPCM predictor) Seeking Sample-accurate Bit depth 16-bit equivalent quality

docs.title: Creating AMS Files
docs.text:
Use the amac CLI tool to encode WAV or MP3 to AMS:

amac -e input.wav output.ams

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• The AMS codec uses a look-ahead buffer and optional noise shaping for improved quality.
  • Block size is configurable at encode time.
  • Supports both loading and streaming.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
{
  "id": 3,
  "name": "compressed_ambience",
  "path": "sounds/ambience.ams",
  "stream": true
}

docs.title: Plugin Codecs
docs.text:
Additional codecs are available as plugins:

Plugin Format Repository Vorbis OGG Vorbis plugin-vorbis FLAC FLAC plugin-flac

Plugin codecs are loaded dynamically at runtime:

Engine::LoadPlugin(AM_OS_STRING("vorbis_plugin"));

docs.title: Codec Selection at Runtime
docs.text:
When loading a sound file, Amplitude automatically selects the appropriate codec based on the file extension and the CanHandleFile() check:

  1. The engine queries each registered codec's CanHandleFile() method.
  2. The first codec that returns true handles the file.
  3. If no codec matches, the load fails with eErrorCode_FileLoadFailed.

Registration order matters if multiple codecs claim the same extension. Register your custom codecs after the built-in ones if you want to override behavior.

docs.title: Memory Pools
docs.text:
All codec allocations use the eMemoryPoolKind_Codec memory pool:

// Good: pool-aware allocation inside your codec
void* buffer = ampoolmalloc(eMemoryPoolKind_Codec, size);

This allows the engine to track codec memory usage and enforce budgets in future versions.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Learn how to write a custom codec.
  • Review the Codec API Reference.
  • Explore the AMS codec tool.

docs.title: Built-in Faders
docs.text: This reference documents the fader curves built into the Amplitude Audio SDK. Faders control how values transition over time for volume, gain, pitch, and other parameters.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Amplitude includes eight built-in faders. All faders use a fast cubic Bézier curve evaluator with fixed endpoints at (0, 0) and (1, 1).

Fader Control Points (x1, y1, x2, y2) Behavior Constant (0, 0, 0, 0) Instant change; no transition. Linear (0, 0, 1, 1) Constant rate of change. Ease (0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1.0) Smooth start and end (CSS default). EaseIn (0.42, 0, 1.0, 1.0) Slow start, fast end. EaseOut (0, 0, 0.58, 1.0) Fast start, slow end. EaseInOut (0.42, 0, 0.58, 1.0) Slow start and end, fast middle. Exponential (0.9, 0.05, 0.95, 0.95) Sharp exponential curve. SCurve (0.4, 0.0, 0.6, 1.0) S-shaped sigmoid curve.

docs.title: Curve Visualization
docs.text:
The seven non-constant faders are cubic Béziers between (0, 0) and (1, 1). The chart below plots each curve over t ∈ [0, 1]. The Constant fader is omitted because it is an instant step rather than a curve.

{ "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json", "description": "Built-in Amplitude fader curves.", "width": "container", "height": 320, "data": { "url": "/static/data/fader-curves.json" }, "mark": { "type": "line", "interpolate": "monotone", "strokeWidth": 2 }, "encoding": { "x": { "field": "x", "type": "quantitative", "title": "t (input)", "scale": { "domain": [0, 1] } }, "y": { "field": "y", "type": "quantitative", "title": "value", "scale": { "domain": [0, 1] } }, "color": { "field": "fader", "type": "nominal", "title": "Fader" } } }

docs.title: Usage in Assets
docs.text: Faders are referenced by name in project assets:

docs.title: Sound Object Fader
docs.text:
{
  "id": 10,
  "name": "explosion",
  "path": "sounds/explosion.wav",
  "fader": "EaseOut"
}

docs.title: Bus Ducking Fade
docs.text:
{
  "duck_buses": [
    {
      "id": 7678456242523,
      "target_gain": 0.3,
      "fade_in": {
        "duration": 200,
        "fader": "EaseIn"
      },
      "fade_out": {
        "duration": 800,
        "fader": "EaseOut"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: RTPC Curve
docs.text:
{
  "curve": {
    "parts": [
      {
        "start": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
        "end": { "x": 1, "y": 1 },
        "fader": "Linear"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Runtime API
docs.text:
You can create fader instances programmatically:

// Get a fader by name
auto fader = Fader::Find("EaseInOut");

// Create an instance
auto instance = fader->CreateInstance();

// Configure the transition
instance->Set(0.0, 1.0, 1000.0); // from 0.0 to 1.0 over 1000 ms
instance->Start(0.0);

// Query the value at a given time
AmReal64 value = instance->GetFromTime(currentTime);

docs.title: When to Use Each Fader
docs.text: Scenario Recommended Fader Reason UI button clicks Constant or Linear Immediate or fast feedback Music crossfades EaseInOut Smooth, natural transition Bus ducking (fade down) EaseIn Gentle reduction Bus ducking (restore) EaseOut Gentle return Explosion impacts Exponential Aggressive, punchy Ambient fade-ins SCurve Slow, imperceptible start Cinematic transitions Ease Balanced, polished feel

docs.title: Custom Faders
docs.text: If the built-in curves do not meet your needs, you can implement a custom fader by subclassing Fader and FaderInstance. See the Custom Fader Tutorial for a step-by-step guide.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Learn how to create a custom fader.
  • Review the Fader API Reference.
  • Explore the Buses Configuration Reference for ducking setup.

docs.title: A
docs.text:
ADPCM — Adaptive Differential Pulse-Code Modulation. A lossy audio compression algorithm used by the AMS codec.

Ambisonics — A full-sphere surround sound technique using spherical harmonics to encode and decode 3D sound fields.

AMIR — Amplitude HRIR file format. An optimized binary format for storing Head-Related Impulse Response data.

AMS — Amplitude Media Stream. Amplitude's custom ADPCM-compressed audio file format.

Attenuation — The reduction of sound level as distance from the source increases.

docs.title: B
docs.text:
B-Format — The channel representation of an Ambisonic signal (W, X, Y, Z, etc.).

Bus — An audio mixing channel that groups sounds together for shared gain, ducking, and effects processing.

docs.title: C
docs.text:
Channel — A single instance of a playing sound in the mixer. Each Play() call creates a channel.

Codec — A software component that encodes and/or decodes audio data from a specific file format.

Collection — A sound object that groups multiple sounds and selects one to play based on a scheduler.

docs.title: D
docs.text:
Decoder — The part of a codec that reads compressed audio data and produces raw PCM samples.

DSP — Digital Signal Processing. Mathematical manipulation of audio signals (filters, effects, etc.).

Ducking — Automatically reducing the gain of one bus when another bus becomes active.

docs.title: E
docs.text:
Encoder — The part of a codec that writes raw PCM samples into a compressed audio file.

Entity — A game object in the Amplitude engine that can emit or receive spatialized audio.

Environment — A zone in 3D space where sounds receive a specific effect (reverb, EQ, etc.).

docs.title: F
docs.text:
Fader — A curve that controls how a value transitions from one point to another over time.

FlatBuffers — A binary serialization format used by Amplitude for project assets and configuration files.

docs.title: H
docs.text:
HRTF — Head-Related Transfer Function. A pair of filters that capture how sound interacts with the human head and ears for 3D spatialization.

HRIR — Head-Related Impulse Response. The time-domain representation of an HRTF.

docs.title: I
docs.text:
ILD — Interaural Level Difference. The difference in sound level between the two ears, used for localization.

ITD — Interaural Time Difference. The difference in arrival time of sound between the two ears, used for localization.

docs.title: L
docs.text:
Listener — A point in 3D space that represents the player's ears. Audio is spatialized relative to listeners.

LZ4 — A fast lossless compression algorithm used by the ampk packager.

docs.title: N
docs.text: Node — A processing unit in the Amplimix pipeline. Nodes perform spatialization, effects, mixing, or dynamics.

docs.title: P
docs.text: Pipeline — A directed acyclic graph (DAG) of nodes that defines how audio is processed in the mixer.

docs.title: R
docs.text:
Resampler — A component that converts audio from one sample rate to another.

Room — A physically modeled acoustic space with walls, materials, and dimensions that affect reverberation.

RTPC — Real-Time Parameter Control. A game value (e.g., speed, health) that dynamically controls audio properties via curves.

docs.title: S
docs.text:
Sound Bank — A binary asset pack that contains multiple sounds, collections, events, and other assets.

Sound Object — A generic term for any playable asset: Sound, Collection, or SwitchContainer.

Spatialization — The process of positioning audio in 3D space using panning, HRTF, or Ambisonics.

Switch Container — A sound object that plays different audio content based on the current state of a switch.

docs.title: V
docs.text:
Virtual Channel — A channel that is not actively mixed but is still tracked by the engine. Virtual channels can be promoted to real channels when resources become available.

Voice — Another term for a channel or sound instance in the mixer.

docs.title: Package Files
docs.text: The .ampk format is Amplitude's package file format for distributing project assets. This reference documents the file structure, compression options, and runtime usage.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An .ampk file is a single binary archive that contains an entire Amplitude project directory. It allows games to ship audio assets as one file instead of thousands of individual files.

Feature Description Format Binary archive with index Compression None or LZ4 Block size Configurable (default 64 KB) Seeking Random access via index Platform All supported platforms

docs.title: Creating Packages
docs.text:
Use the ampk CLI tool:

# Uncompressed (fastest loading)
ampk ./my_project/ output.ampk

# LZ4 compressed (smaller file)
ampk -c 1 -b 128 ./my_project/ output.ampk

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
AMPK Header
├── Magic number (4 bytes): "AMPK"
├── Version (2 bytes)
├── Compression mode (1 byte)
├── Block size (4 bytes)
├── Entry count (4 bytes)
│
Entry Index
├── Entry 1: path hash, offset, compressed size, uncompressed size
├── Entry 2: path hash, offset, compressed size, uncompressed size
├── ...
│
Data Blocks
├── Block 1: compressed or raw data
├── Block 2: compressed or raw data
├── ...

docs.title: Runtime Loading
docs.text:
At runtime, use PackageFileSystem to load assets from an .ampk file:

// Create a package file system
auto packageFs = std::make_shared<PackageFileSystem>();
packageFs->SetBasePath(AM_OS_STRING("assets/audio.pak"));
packageFs->StartOpenFileSystem();
while (!packageFs->TryFinalizeOpenFileSystem())
    Thread::Sleep(1);

// Set it as the engine's file system
amEngine->SetFileSystem(packageFs);

The engine will then load all assets (sound banks, configs, etc.) from the package transparently.

docs.title: Compression Modes
docs.text:
Mode Value Ratio Decompression Speed Uncompressed 0 1.0 N/A (direct read) LZ4 1 ~2.0–3.0× Very fast

LZ4 is recommended for mobile and console builds where storage space is limited. Desktop builds may prefer uncompressed packages for the fastest possible load times on SSDs.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Group projects by platform: Create separate packages for each platform if asset sets differ.
  • Use uncompressed for streaming: LZ4 decompression adds a small CPU cost; uncompressed is better for streamed music.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Review the ampk CLI tool reference.
  • Explore the PackageFileSystem API Reference.

docs.title: Built-in Pipeline Nodes
docs.text: This reference documents every built-in pipeline node in the Amplitude Audio SDK. Pipeline nodes are the building blocks of the audio processing graph executed by Amplimix each frame.

docs.title: Node Categories
docs.text:
All nodes fall into one of four categories:

Category Description Input Marks the entry point of audio into the pipeline. Output Marks the exit point of processed audio. Processor Transforms audio in-place (single input, single output). Mixer Combines multiple inputs into one output.

docs.title: InputNode
docs.text:
Marks the start of the pipeline. Receives audio from the sound source.

{ "id": 1, "name": "Input", "consume": [] }

docs.title: OutputNode
docs.text:
Marks the end of the pipeline. Sends audio to the audio device.

{ "id": 99, "name": "Output", "consume": [98] }

docs.title: AttenuationNode
docs.text:
Applies distance-based gain attenuation using the sound's assigned attenuation model.

Parameter Type Description attenuation float Output gain after applying the curve (read-only). 
{ "id": 2, "name": "Attenuation", "consume": [1] }

docs.title: StereoPanningNode
docs.text:
Pans mono sources to stereo left/right based on azimuth angle.

{ "id": 3, "name": "StereoPanning", "consume": [2] }

docs.title: AmbisonicPanningNode
docs.text:
Encodes a mono source into Ambisonic B-Format channels based on 3D position.

{ "id": 4, "name": "AmbisonicPanning", "consume": [2] }

docs.title: AmbisonicRotatorNode
docs.text:
Rotates the Ambisonic sound field to match listener orientation.

{ "id": 5, "name": "AmbisonicRotator", "consume": [4] }

docs.title: AmbisonicBinauralDecoderNode
docs.text:
Decodes Ambisonic B-Format to binaural stereo using HRIR convolution.

{ "id": 6, "name": "AmbisonicBinauralDecoder", "consume": [5] }

docs.title: AmbisonicMixerNode
docs.text:
Mixes multiple Ambisonic streams together.

{ "id": 7, "name": "AmbisonicMixer", "consume": [5, 10] }

docs.title: StereoMixerNode
docs.text:
Mixes multiple stereo streams together.

{ "id": 8, "name": "StereoMixer", "consume": [3, 6] }

docs.title: EnvironmentEffectNode
docs.text:
Applies the environment's assigned effect to sounds inside the zone.

{ "id": 9, "name": "EnvironmentEffect", "consume": [2] }

docs.title: NearFieldEffectNode
docs.text:
Simulates near-field pressure effects for very close sources.

{ "id": 10, "name": "NearFieldEffect", "consume": [2] }

docs.title: ReflectionsNode
docs.text:
Computes early reflections based on room geometry.

{ "id": 11, "name": "Reflections", "consume": [1] }

docs.title: ReverbNode
docs.text:
Applies late reverberation based on room materials and dimensions.

{ "id": 12, "name": "Reverb", "consume": [1] }

docs.title: OcclusionNode
docs.text:
Applies frequency-dependent low-pass filtering based on the entity's occlusion value.

{ "id": 13, "name": "Occlusion", "consume": [2] }

docs.title: ObstructionNode
docs.text:
Applies low-pass filtering based on the entity's obstruction value.

{ "id": 14, "name": "Obstruction", "consume": [2] }

docs.title: LimiterNode
docs.text:
Prevents clipping by limiting peak amplitude.

Parameter Type Description threshold dB Level above which limiting begins. attack ms Time to respond to peaks. release ms Time to return to unity gain. 
{ "id": 15, "name": "Limiter", "consume": [8] }

docs.title: ClampNode
docs.text:
Hard-clips samples to a maximum amplitude.

{ "id": 16, "name": "Clamp", "consume": [15] }

docs.title: HardClipNode
docs.text:
Applies aggressive hard clipping (distortion).

{ "id": 17, "name": "HardClip", "consume": [15] }

docs.title: RoundoffClipNode
docs.text:
Applies softer roundoff clipping.

{ "id": 18, "name": "RoundoffClip", "consume": [15] }

docs.title: Default Pipeline
docs.text:
The default pipeline shipped with Amplitude combines most of these nodes:

{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "default",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": 1, "name": "Input", "consume": [] },
    { "id": 2, "name": "Attenuation", "consume": [1] },
    { "id": 3, "name": "Occlusion", "consume": [2] },
    { "id": 4, "name": "StereoPanning", "consume": [17] },
    { "id": 5, "name": "AmbisonicPanning", "consume": [3] },
    { "id": 6, "name": "NearFieldEffect", "consume": [3] },
    { "id": 7, "name": "AmbisonicMixer", "consume": [18] },
    { "id": 8, "name": "StereoMixer", "consume": [4, 6, 10, 12, 14] },
    { "id": 10, "name": "AmbisonicBinauralDecoder", "consume": [7] },
    { "id": 11, "name": "Reflections", "consume": [1] },
    { "id": 12, "name": "AmbisonicBinauralDecoder", "consume": [11] },
    { "id": 13, "name": "HardClip", "consume": [8] },
    { "id": 14, "name": "Reverb", "consume": [1] },
    { "id": 15, "name": "Obstruction", "consume": [3] },
    { "id": 16, "name": "EnvironmentEffect", "consume": [3] },
    { "id": 17, "name": "StereoMixer", "consume": [15, 16] },
    { "id": 18, "name": "AmbisonicRotator", "consume": [5] },
    { "id": 9, "name": "Output", "consume": [13] }
  ]
}

docs.title: Custom Nodes
docs.text: You can implement custom pipeline nodes by subclassing Node and NodeInstance. See the Custom Pipeline Node Tutorial for details.
